text: The 2021 tree-cover loss of 81.3 hectares in the asset was legal. The loss occurred in a planted forest area (68.1 ha) dominated by pine species (*Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*), not native forest, which is explicitly allowed under Uruguay’s forestry regulations. Additionally, no native forest was affected (0.0 ha). While 13.2 ha of the loss occurred outside mapped forest zones, this does not necessarily imply illegality, as the land may have been previously cleared or designated for other uses. The event was confirmed by multiple sources (Hansen GFC and JRC GFC2020), and the size of the loss (81.3 ha) did not trigger illegal thresholds under Uruguayan law, which primarily restricts clearing of native forests.
